title: The Prophetic Monument
paragraphs: “Um…”

The High Priest looked around at us with a troubled expression. He seemed a bit unreliable. Almost like someone raised in a sheltered environment. Well, if he tries anything suspicious, he can take a one-way trip to the afterlife.
“Well, well, we might as well take a look. Maybe we’ll be able to read it.”
“There are also texts written in the so-called ‘Hero Script,’ the language of the heroes’ world. There may be useful information for you, Heroes.”
“Motoyasu, do you know anything about this?”
“This is my first time coming here.”
“Then it might be worth checking out.”
We stood up. The High Priest began leading the way, saying, “This way.” The Filolial and the rivals looked slightly bored. Father was also bored.
With that thought in mind, we continued walking through the large church. Every so often, some church members would glance at us with great curiosity.
“How do you plan to enter the castle? If you’d like, our church can arrange a grand triumphant return for you.”
“I’d rather not attract too much attention.”
“Yes, while we appreciate the gesture…”
Ren and Itsuki weren’t fond of standing out too much. I rather liked the attention. What about Father?

“Motoyasu-kun has a plan, and it would be troublesome if we got caught up in any unnecessary conspiracies or if our faces became too well-known. So, for now… If we’re going to do something like that, could we wait until we have more leeway?”
“Understood. Yes. Then, if the opportunity arises, please do consider it.”

He was surprisingly reasonable. The Four Heroes Church generally didn’t go against the Four Holy Heroes, so there shouldn’t be any issues… right? Well, according to Father, organizations tend to become corrupt over time, so this High Priest was probably a schemer in his own way. At least from what we had seen so far, he seemed relatively mild-mannered.
“This way.”
We were led to a basement room.
“It’s so cramped!”
Rival was struggling to fit through the narrow passage. Serves him right. He can just stay stuck there by himself.
“Then, Gaelion-chan, would you mind waiting upstairs?”
“No! Gaelion wants to stay with Father!”
“That may be, but… there’s something important down here, apparently…”
As Father scratched his cheek in hesitation, Assistant and Mole tried to soothe Rival.
“Gaelion, be patient. In return, I’ll wait with you.”
“I will too…”
“Uu… alright… Gaelion will be patient…”
“Good boy. Then Wyndia-chan, Imiya-chan, I’ll leave him to you.”
“Yes.”
And so, the rivals ended up waiting outside partway through. The room we were led into looked like a graveyard. There were bookshelves in each of the four corners.
“I never expected the Four Heroes Church to have a place like this…” Éclair muttered.
Even knights don’t know everything, it seems, even if it’s about another country.
“This is a sanctuary known only to the High Priests, passed down through generations. Yes.”
“Hmm… Leaving aside the Heroes, is it really alright for someone like me to enter such a sacred place?”

“The prophet left these inscriptions so that the Heroes would have aid in their battle against the waves of calamity. And as the waves mentioned in the prophecy are indeed occurring, I believe that those who accompany the Heroes have the right to see them as well. Yes.”
“I see… In that case, I shall take this as a rare opportunity.”
While Éclair and the others discussed, I looked around the room. She spoke highly of this “sanctuary,” but for a so-called sacred place, it was rather unimpressive.
“Please take a look at these stone monuments.”

When I turned to look, I saw several stone tablets lined up. However, many had cracks or missing pieces. Even if we could understand the writing, wouldn’t it be difficult to read them in this condition?
“They’re in pretty bad shape. Have they been properly maintained?”
“Motoyasu… Why do you always have to be so provocative…” Ren sighed in exasperation.
I understood his point, but if they’re in this state, there’s no way we could read them even if we wanted to.
“For that, I can only offer my deepest apologies. While age is a factor, it is said that a former High Priest a few generations ago lost his mind and damaged the inscriptions… Yes.”
“Then doesn’t that mean they’re unreadable…?”
This sounded familiar. Just like with the inscriptions at the sites where the Spirit Tortoise and Phoenix were sealed. Given their age, I suppose it can’t be helped.
“In any case, would you please take a look? Each inscription corresponds to a specific Hero, with their respective weapon marks on them.”
“I have a bad feeling that there might be a trap…”
“Well, there’s no helping it. I’ll go check it out.”

I stepped in front of the stone monument engraved with the mark of the spear. It seemed to have a lot written on it. As I tried to follow the inscriptions with my eyes… what is this? The letters were shifting around, making them unreadable.
“Oh?”

As I tilted my head in confusion, the gemstone in my spear began to glow, and the spear engraving on the monument lit up. Then, the letters themselves started shining, making them readable. Since they were glowing, the missing parts didn’t affect the text. And on top of that, they were in Japanese—the so-called “Hero’s Script” of this world.
Or rather, the content of the glowing letters was different from the ones that had originally been written. Was this some kind of trick to ensure only Heroes could read the true message?
“This is… As expected of the Heroes. Yes.”
The High Priest let out a voice of admiration. It seemed that, unlike with the Spirit Tortoise and Phoenix, there was no lost knowledge this time.

As I pondered this, the glowing text, which had been several lines long, began to disappear, leaving only the second row intact. However, some kind of magical trace remained, leaving behind black markings, so I could still read it. Alright… The second row is still glowing, but I’ll start from the first row.

“To the one who makes these letters shine: Your birth was one of misfortune. Your father hails from another world, and one day, the mystery of your birth will be revealed in this world. To pursue this mystery, seeking the Dragon Emperor is the fastest path. Your ability to see through conspiracies is worthy of praise. With your sharp, spear-like insight, purge the corruption of the monarchy and save the world from the threat of the waves.”
…Who is this talking about? This has absolutely nothing to do with me. My parents were completely normal people.

Born into misfortune? I have no recollection of that whatsoever. If anything, until I was killed by those pigs, I thought of myself as incredibly fortunate. Looking back now, I find myself utterly foolish.
“Motoyasu, was your birth unfortunate?”
“I have no idea.”
“Isn’t the glowing second row the part meant for Motoyasu-san?”
“Ah, maybe it’s meant for a predecessor or something?”

I see. The reason it didn’t sound familiar at all is probably because it has nothing to do with me. Come to think of it, there were other Four Holy Heroes summoned before us, so this might be their monument. With that in mind, I started reading the glowing second row.

“To the one who makes these letters shine: The trust you desire upon coming to this world is a noble thing. However, that trust will only bring you fortune if placed in those truly worthy of it. Be careful not to mistake who you put your faith in, lest you fall victim to conspiracy, bringing further calamity and extinguishing the light of the Hero meant to save this world. So long as you believe in the messenger from the heavens and continue to fight, your future will be one of brilliance.”

That’s what was written. How unexpected… There are quite a few parts that resonate with me. Believing in that pig and suffering for it—there’s a lot that hits close to home. And then, a little further away, there was still more text continuing.
“…If you are reading these words, then you have walked this same path many times before. If you seek salvation for this world, accept the painful choice.”

The text ended there and moved on to the next paragraph. Hmm, this was supposedly written by some prophet, but it might actually be the real deal. Compared to something like bloodline divination, this was far more credible.
“So? What do you think?”
“It feels oddly accurate, somehow.”
